paper_title: Hunting Dark Matter Lines in the Infrared Background with the James Webb Space Telescope
notes: Paper presents new measured exclusion limits on axion-photon coupling g_agamma from JWST NIRSpec IFU observations of blank sky in the mass range 0.8–3 eV. The primary result is shown in Figure 2 (bottom panel) as 2σ power-constrained limits on g_agamma vs. mass m_a. Key numerical values extracted from text: τ < 6.7×10^26 s at m_DM ≃ 0.9 eV (corresponding to g_agamma > 9.4×10^-12 GeV^-1 at m_a = 2.15 eV), and g_agamma > 2.4×10^-11 GeV^-1 for m_a = 1 eV. The paper uses the continuum model constraint (red curve in Fig. 2), which is more sensitive than the total flux limit. Data points are read from Figure 2 (bottom) at representative masses. The search targets decaying dark matter producing narrow infrared emission lines via the dimension-5 operator L = -(1/4)g_agamma a F_μν F̃^μν. No local DM density assumption is needed as this is an astrophysical/cosmological bound using the Milky Way halo profile (NFW with ρ_s = 0.18 GeV/cm³), not a dedicated haloscope experiment. Confidence level is 2σ (95% CL) as stated in the paper. | selector: text (sole candidate)
